profile.entities: Vardhman Special Steels Ltd (Ludhiana, Punjab); Aichi Steel Corporation (strategic partner & shareholder — Technical Assistance Agreement signed this quarter for the forging unit); planned **non-Aichi JV for the Advanced Metals division** (aerospace/nuclear, partner not yet selected)
profile.mgmt: Sachit Jain (Chairman & Managing Director); R.K. Rewari (Executive Director); Sanjeev Singla (CFO)
profile.subseg: Automotive alloy steel; non-automotive specialty steel (die steels, railway axles, windmill shafts); precision forged components; future: advanced metals (aerospace, nuclear)

bull_bear.body: Funding for the greenfield was addressed directly and confidently: cash already received, an **equity raise planned "sometime next year"** sized to need, with **both large shareholders — Vardhman Group and Aichi — having committed to put in as much capital as required**, plus institutional appetite and available bank debt. The Punjab government is described as "very keen" on the project with support "fully assured." The forging project's >10% cost saving (from a INR475cr base) came from renegotiated terms and substituting Indian equipment for Japanese. No dividend or buyback discussion.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Licence ceiling is the binding constraint.** Growth is capped at ~7–8% until the 3.6-lakh-tonne EC arrives. Management repeated the honest caveat twice: "you haven't got it until you have got it… fingers crossed."
- **Greenfield cost inflation.** Iran-war-driven metal prices and rupee depreciation push cost per tonne up; the scope increase pushes total cost up further. The FY30 commissioning date has not moved yet — watch whether it does.
- **Long dated payback.** The forging plant commissions Q4 FY28 but contributes revenue only from FY30; the greenfield commissions FY30 with revenue FY31. Nothing in the current capex programme materially changes earnings before FY29.
- **Export assumptions already proved wrong.** Management admitted the direct-export thesis was an error — "we had erred. We made a mistake in our assumptions" — and exports will cap near 10%. Customers want Indian *components*, not Indian steel, which is the actual rationale for the forging plant.
- **Advanced Metals is directional only.** No partner, no timeline beyond "a couple of years," and management explicitly told analysts not to model it.
- **Equity dilution ahead** in FY28 for the greenfield.
- **Q1 price settlements incomplete** — some OEMs have not accepted the increase; the Q1 number may be revised upward with the spill-over landing in Q2, which flatters Q2 optically.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Among the most credible in this batch. Sachit Jain volunteered a downward adjustment to his own EBITDA figure to strip out non-operating treasury income, publicly admitted the export forecast was a mistake, corrected an analyst who mis-stated the greenfield as 5 *million* tonnes with self-deprecating humour ("we have no plans to be big, big boys"), repeatedly caveated the EC approval as not-yet-in-hand, and told investors that the Advanced Metals numbers are too small to bother modelling — the opposite of the usual incentive. He publicly credited the operating team for productivity gains that exceeded what management had thought possible. Guidance is given as ranges with named drivers and revised only with reasoning attached. The one soft spot: no disclosure of net debt, cash, or the funding quantum for the greenfield.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The 7–8% growth optics are an artefact of the licence, not of demand. The company is turning orders away and examining outsourced rolling of imported billets to serve customers it cannot supply. Any read of VSSL as a low-growth business misreads a regulatory cap as a demand cap.
- The die-steel move is a realisation story, not a volume story: INR2.5–4 lakh/tonne against a current INR85,000/tonne average, achieved *within* the same 3-lakh-tonne licence. Mix shift is the only growth lever available until the EC lands — which is precisely why ingot casting is being rushed into Q3 FY27.
- The real reason for the forging plant is hidden in the export answer: customers want to buy *components* from India, not steel. The forging unit converts a failed direct-export thesis into an indirect-export franchise. Management has committed to start estimating indirect exports from next quarter — a new disclosure to watch for.
- Seeding non-automotive products now is explicitly about *filling the greenfield faster* later. The FY28 die-steel volumes matter less than the qualifications they generate.
- Green steel is quietly becoming the strongest moat: OEM 2030 targets plus a sole-qualified-supplier position converts an ESG line item into pricing and allocation power, already visible in the Toyota Kirloskar Sambhaji Nagar pull.
- Aichi's surplus funds sitting in Indian money markets are generating enough income that management had to strip it out of EBITDA — an unusual quality-of-earnings tell, disclosed voluntarily.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Strategic financial guardrail of peak debt/equity "≤ 0.75x — discipline preserved through the cycle" alongside the ~₹2,600 Cr FY26–30 committed capex.
- The Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 3.50 per share on fully paid-up equity shares, subject to approval at the Annual General Meeting.
- Capital-raising history cited: Rights Issue of Rs 67.85 Cr (April 2017), QIP of Rs 50 Cr (Feb 2018), bonus share issue in 1:1 ratio (May 2023), and Aichi Steel raising its stake to 24.90% (Jun 2025).
- Balance sheet as on 31st Mar'26 shows equity of INR 1,277.32 Cr, non-current borrowings of 0.00 and current borrowings of 92.65 Cr (versus equity 797.91 Cr and borrowings 3.29 / 116.43 Cr as on 31st Mar'25).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Automotive alloy steel** — the sole current growth engine, running at licensed capacity. Maruti is ~10% of business today and is the deliberate concentration target going forward; management stressed there is no current customer-concentration risk. The Aichi tie-up delivered global Toyota approval and is delivering the Maruti localisation of imported steels.
- **Non-automotive specialty steel (engine two)** — the FY27–28 build. Route is **ingot casting**, being installed by Q3 FY27. Target products: **die steels** (India imports ~INR1,000cr worth annually), **railway axles**, **windmill shafts** — all import-substitution plays. Economics are transformative on realisation: current average price ~INR85,000/t versus **INR2.5 lakh/t for non-ESR die steel and INR3.5–4 lakh/t as ESR**, though management cautioned costs are also much higher (heat treatment, pressing) so margin does not scale proportionally. Critically, Aichi makes die steels in-house for its own forging (~50% share of the Japanese forging market, 150–170kt), so the know-how is tried and tested.
- **Forging (engine three)** — Technical Assistance Agreement with Aichi Steel signed this quarter; project on schedule and under budget. Ramp will be "very gradual" because it is a new business, but shortened because Vardhman already sends steel to Aichi, gets it forged in Japan and sends the forged product to customers for approval — so process approvals will pre-exist commissioning.
- **Advanced Metals (engine four)** — aerospace and nuclear-plant steels, ~1.5 years away from starting. Explicitly a **non-Aichi JV** (Aichi is strong in automotive, stainless/medical and die steels but not here). Partner search will "take a couple of years"; a separate company because "nobody is going to pass their know-how without being an equal partner." Management pre-emptively told analysts these numbers are "too small and a little outside your horizon."
- **Green steel** — carbon footprint below 0.5 with the necessary approvals, which management claims makes VSSL the **only Indian company able to supply approved green steel**. Toyota Kirloskar's new Sambhaji Nagar (Aurangabad) plant is cited as a specific pull, and most OEMs have 2030 green-steel targets.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Green-steel monopoly, claimed and specific.** "Our carbon footprint is below 0.5… there isn't any other company which is near us in carbon footprint, which has the approvals." Two commercial consequences were evidenced: a strong position for European exports, and being the only qualified supplier for Toyota Kirloskar's expansion. With OEM 2030 targets, this is a widening rather than static advantage.
- **Aichi Steel as a technology and approval channel.** Global Toyota approval and the Maruti localisation mandate were both attributed directly to the partnership. For die steels specifically, foreign know-how is described as essential, and Aichi has it in production use.
- **Renewable cost position.** 43% of power from solar with a further ~50% capacity expansion planned — a structural cost advantage in an energy-intensive process.
- **Pricing pass-through structure.** OEM contracts move price up or down with raw-material cost, which is *why* the company can guide an EBITDA/tonne band at all: "We remain protected within a range."

business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: The EBITDA/tonne band is the company's core disclosure discipline, and it is being ratcheted up on four identified levers. Already delivered: the new reheating furnace has improved yields, and the Kocks Block plus reheating furnace took the rolling mill to its 3-lakh-tonne input capacity. Still to come: NDT and peeling lines in-house from Sept/Oct 2026, which eliminates outside job work from Q3 FY27; the solar expansion in ~1–1.5 years; and volume-driven fixed-cost dilution. The pricing mechanism protects the band rather than expanding it — OEMs reset prices on cost parameters, so raw-material inflation flows through rather than compressing margin, with a lag. One caveat management gave on the greenfield: metal prices are up globally and the rupee has depreciated because of the Iran war, so **cost per tonne on the new plant may come in "maybe a little higher"** than envisaged even as scale rises.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Volume 59,000t (+6.5%); revenue INR486cr (+12%); EBITDA INR68cr; **EBITDA/t INR10,760 (INR10,700 ex-Aichi treasury income) — top of the INR8,000–11,000 band**; PAT INR41cr vs INR20cr YoY and INR34cr QoQ. Solar delivered a full quarter, 43% of power, 2.3cr units; carbon footprint <0.5. **Technical Assistance Agreement signed with Aichi for the forging unit; project cost >10% below the INR475cr estimate.** EC application filed for melting 3.0 → 3.6 lakh t. Rolling mill at licensed 3-lakh-tonne capacity; team confident of 330,000t input. Completely booked out and refusing orders. **Guidance raised: FY28 EBITDA/t band to INR8,000–12,000, FY29 intended at INR9,000–12,000.** Greenfield being re-scoped larger (scrap preheating, more continuous testing lines) — revised project to next board meeting; land/machinery to be finalised by end-Aug/mid-Sept 2026. Export thesis publicly corrected — direct exports cap ~10%; indirect exports via components to be estimated from next quarter.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: did the 3.6-lakh-tonne EC approval arrive within the promised 3–4 months (the single biggest unlock); were the NDT and peeling lines commissioned by Sept/Oct; is ingot casting on track for Q3; did Q2 realisations rise as committed and did the Q1 OEM settlement spill over; European OEM commercial supply started in H2; greenfield land/machinery finalised by mid-Sept and at what revised capacity and cost; FY27 volume tracking to 255,000t._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Volume:** **~255,000 t for FY27**; **>270,000 t in FY28**, rising to **~290,000 t in FY28 if the environmental clearance lands** (production can improve to that level without further capex); **330,000–340,000 t by FY29** once new capex is installed.
- **Margin (the headline commitment):** EBITDA/t range moves from the current **INR8,000–11,000 to INR8,000–12,000 in FY28**, and management intends to raise the floor to **INR9,000–12,000 in FY29** once the new solar plant commissions. Four named drivers: (i) fixed-cost dilution on higher volume, (ii) operating costs already falling, (iii) job work / outside processing coming in-house **from Q3 FY27**, (iv) new solar capacity ~a year out.
- **Pricing:** **Q2 FY27 realisations will be higher than Q1** — a price increase has been sought effective 1 July. Q1 settlements are incomplete with some OEMs and are "likely to rise higher," with the spill-over landing in Q2. Q3 expected flat to marginally either way, depending on raw material.
- **Capex / commissioning dates:**
  - **New NDT line and new peeling line — commissioned by September/October 2026.** These remove the current bottleneck (finished material piling up awaiting testing capacity, and peeling being job-worked outside).
  - **Ingot casting — established by Q3 FY27, stabilised by Q4 FY27**; enables **regular die-steel production in FY28**.
  - **Environmental clearance for melting capacity 3.0 → 3.6 lakh t — approval expected "in the next 3, 4 months."**
  - **Forging unit (with Aichi) — commissioning in Q4 FY28**; 6–12 months to fill the plant; **revenue from end-FY29 / FY30**. **Project cost more than 10% below the INR475cr estimate.**
  - **Greenfield steel plant (Punjab, 5 lakh t, being upsized) — land and machinery to be finalised by end-August, latest mid-September 2026**; **commissioning FY30 (financial year '29-'30)**; 6–8 months to stabilise; **revenues from FY31**.
  - **Solar plant capacity +~50% in about 1 to 1.5 years** (savings per unit lower than phase 1 because of new domestic-cell content rules).
  - **European OEM commercial supply — expected in H2 FY27** ("later part of this financial year"); samples already sent.
  - **Maruti import-substitution commercial production — starts Q4 FY27.**
- **Capital raising:** an equity raise **"sometime next year"** (FY28), timing dependent on funding need. Vardhman Group and Aichi have both committed to subscribe as required; institutional appetite exists; debt described as available.
- **Exports:** deliberately capped — "At max, it will go up to about 10%."
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: There is no order book by design: "we never have a strong output — there is no system of a very strong order book… no customer gives long-term orders." The relevant statement is the inverse — the company is **completely booked out and refusing orders**, and is "finding it difficult to meet the requirements of the customers." Management is even examining importing billets and rolling them on job work outside to service demand it cannot make in-house, contingent on finding a credible supply chain. The next identified volume step-up is Maruti import substitution beginning commercial production in Q4 FY27.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: The four-engine framing is the cleanest strategic articulation on the call: (1) automotive steel today, (2) non-automotive specialty steel from FY28, (3) forging from FY29–30, (4) advanced metals ~1.5 years out and beyond. The non-obvious purpose of engine two was stated plainly — volumes will be low initially, but **seeding these products now means the new 5-lakh-tonne plant can be filled faster** once it commissions, because the business will already be established and qualified.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: The best quarter in the company's history on unit economics — EBITDA/tonne of INR10,760 (INR10,700 excluding non-operating Aichi surplus-fund income) sits at the top of the guided INR8,000–11,000 band, and PAT of INR41cr doubled YoY. The constraint is now regulatory, not commercial: demand is so strong the company is "refusing orders" and running the rolling mill at its 3-lakh-tonne licensed ceiling while the team believes 330,000 tonnes is physically achievable. Management raised the FY28 EBITDA/t band to INR8,000–12,000 and flagged INR9,000–12,000 the year after, and disclosed that the INR475cr forging project will cost **more than 10% less** than budgeted.
